extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, journal editors, and researchers who perform manuscript review
extracted.subtask_description: Normative and operational standards for scientific referees describing what reviewers should do, how they should judge manuscripts, and the ethical/procedural tensions they must manage when deciding community recognition for work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinterestedness
rubrics_metrics.description: The referee gains no personal recognition and must not be motivated by competition with the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recuse where personal stakes (priority competition, school disagreement, career rivalry) would compromise disinterestedness; avoid using review to advance one's own recognition or to disadvantage competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgements should be based on the merits of the contribution alone, not on the author's identity, school, or status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the manuscript as if the author were anonymous to enforce universalism; do not let prestige or institutional affiliation affect assessment of quality or originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communality
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge is to be shared; refereeing must not be used to suppress findings the referee dislikes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid withholding publication for non-scientific motives; uphold norms that the community's knowledge should be disseminated rather than hoarded or suppressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organised scepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Every claim should be subject to systematic critical scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply systematic, rigorous critical evaluation to methods, data, and inferences rather than cursory or ad hoc commentary; balance scepticism with fairness to novel claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists (and referees) must reach their own judgements free of authority pressure; reviewers should not defer to senior authors or to an editor's expected verdict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resist deference to prominent figures or editorial expectations; provide independent judgment even when it contradicts perceived community leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that empirical claims are supported by evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine data, methods, and logic to verify that conclusions are warranted by the presented evidence; point out methodological flaws and unsupported inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that priority claims are not duplicated and that the work is genuinely novel where claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty relative to existing literature; report potential priority conflicts and notify editors if the referee or others have prior claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the work addresses a question the field considers important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh the contribution's significance to the discipline and whether it advances debates or solves meaningful problems; consider importance relative to journal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Fit the manuscript to the scope and audience of the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper's topic, level, and claims match the intended readership and mission of the target journal; recommend rejection, transfer, or revision accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicitly rank the contribution's importance through differential journal placement; referees help allocate recognition via placement decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly weigh whether the contribution merits the recognition the journal would confer (senior journals confer more recognition and demand a higher bar of significance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialisation vs generalist judgement (tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrow specialists may be most competent but most biased; generalists are more disinterested but less competent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the trade-off when selecting reviewers and when evaluating reviews: combine specialist technical checks with broader, disinterested perspectives to reach balanced decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality vs solidity (tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees must trade off the value of risky, novel claims against the importance of consolidative, careful work; disciplines tend toward conservatism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately consider whether to favor innovation or careful verification; avoid reflexively rejecting highly original work for lack of immediate solidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition allocation vs error correction (tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: A referee emphasizing whether the paper 'advanced the field' may overlook errors, while one focusing on error correction may downplay importance; these aims can conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of which function you are prioritizing in a given review and try to balance advancing promising ideas with ensuring methodological soundness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate as if the author were anonymous (operational norm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the manuscript on its merits by imagining author anonymity to support universalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use anonymity as a heuristic to reduce bias from author identity, but still disclose known conflicts if true anonymity is impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recusal for personal stakes (operational norm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees should recuse themselves when personal stakes would compromise disinterestedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in competition with the author, belonging to rival schools, or having career-related conflicts, inform the editor and decline to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report potential priority conflicts (operational norm)
rubrics_metrics.description: The referee should report where they or others might have prior claim to the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose personal or close-colleague prior work that affects impartiality; notify editors of possible overlapping claims to allow editors to manage conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise the limited remit of review (humility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees are deciding whether the community should grant recognition, not pronouncing absolute truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame recommendations in terms of suitability for recognition/publication rather than definitive statements of truth; be modest about what a single review can establish.
